messages:
Ava (Design): Quick design thread — proposing a compact axis treatment for small-screen dashboards + a consistent spike-handling policy. TL;DR: reduce axis verbosity, collapse unit labels on condensed view, and visually de-emphasize isolated spikes with a micro-annotation instead of rescaling. Thoughts?

Leo (PM): Short-term win for mobile dashboards. Main question: are we at risk of hiding important regressions by de-emphasizing spikes? :thinking_face:

Maya (Data Viz): Agree with caution. Proposal: don't remove spikes — mark them. Behaviour: smoothing applies only to points within 1.5x IQR, smoothing alpha 0.25 by default. If point > median*3 (or > 3x recent rolling median) it gets an outlier marker + subtle pulsing halo.

Sam (Frontend): Implementation note: add a chart config "axisMode: 'compact' | 'expanded'". In compact mode we show major ticks only, unit suffix collapsed to a single header (e.g., "RPS") with aria-hidden on individual tick labels. Need accessible expansion control.

Priya (Accessibility): Copy nit: avoid 'compact' for users who might not know what it does. Suggest label 'Simplified axis (toggle)'. Ensure keyboard focus reveals full tick value and timestamp tooltip. Also color contrast for the outlier halo must meet AA.

Ava (Design): Good call on copy. 'Simplified axis' reads clearer. UX flow: default to simplified on small widths, but show a persistent expand affordance. Micro-annotation idea: a tiny chevron + "+n spikes" indicator when spikes are collapsed.

Maya (Data Viz): For the visual spec: dashed faint line for smoothed curve, solid for raw. Outlier marker: 4px filled circle with 1px stroke, color variant of highlight. Hover shows "Spike: +123% vs median". Also add example rule: if a spike lasts > 3 samples, treat it as trend (do not hide).

Sam (Frontend): Quick pseudo:
```
const isOutlier = v => v > rollingMedian(window=20)*3;
if (isOutlier(point)) markOutlier(point)
else applyEWMA(points, alpha=0.25)
```
I'll prototype with canvas overlay for markers so we don't disrupt performance.

Leo (PM): Can we A/B the two defaults? Beta customers with high-cardinality charts might prefer expanded. @ops any config flags we can use to gate?

ops (Infra): We can gate via feature-flag: chart.compact_axis rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Need an experiment key.

Priya (Accessibility): Also request: add automated axe/checks for the expanded tooltip content and ensure screen reader can announce "outlier at 2026-05-01 14:12: value 4,320, 3x median".

Ava (Design): Next steps: Sam to drop prototype, Maya to add viz testcases (3 dashboards: low-noise, high-noise, trend-with-spikes), Priya to write a11y acceptance, Leo to own rollout plan. We'll reconvene in 48h. :thumbsup:

Sam (Frontend): Prototype in flight, aiming EOD.

Maya (Data Viz): I'll upload test CSVs and a mock panel.

deploy-bot: New frontend branch "compact-axis-prop" created and CI queued.

Leo (PM): Thanks — excited to see the prototype. :eyes:
